answer_1.quote: We select three common NLG tasks: summarization (including news and dialogue), paraphrase, and table-to-text generation ... We sample one example from each of the four datasets (CNN/Dailymail, SAMSum, News Commentary, and WebNLG) ... the data we use is in English.
answer_1.outputs: generated summaries, dialogues, paraphrases, and table-to-text descriptions

answer_2.quote: Table shows the performance of six commonly used non-LLM evaluation metrics as baselines, including BLEU, CHRF++, ROUGE, COMET-QE, BERTScore, and BLEURT.

answer_3.quote: Our tests cover both proprietary LLMs (GPT-3.5 and GPT-4) and open-source LLMs (Prometheus) ... We prompt the model to evaluate all the perturbed texts, as well as the original text, in the form of scoring.

answer_4.quote: We recruit 40 annotators (each of whom is proficient in English ...) ... each piece of data is annotated four times ... the annotators are shown two texts simultaneously ... and asked to judge their quality relationship based on the given description of the quality criterion.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators evaluate the quality of texts according to detailed aspect definitions and criteria provided in the prompts.
